items.name: Here's where voters are rejecting data centers on midterm ballots (full list)
items.headline: Here's where voters are rejecting data centers on midterm ballots (full list)
items.claim: On 2026-11-03 voters rejected or restricted data centers in dozens of communities across at least seven states: Ohio had 21 measures with 13 municipal bans (some only above 25 MW) and over 80% of Ashville voters rejecting a facility under construction; six Illinois municipalities voted against; bans or moratoria also passed in Kansas, Maine, California and Florida towns. No aggregate GW printed.

items.name: Ohio and Georgia local votes hit named hyperscaler projects (Data Centers: Daily Notes, Nov 4)
items.source: writing.strisker.com (aggregator of local press) and TokenPost - secondary
items.headline: Ohio and Georgia local votes hit named hyperscaler projects (Data Centers: Daily Notes, Nov 4)
items.candidate_dial: GW deferral (named projects: AMZN, META, Vantage, OpenAI)
items.claim: Trenton OH Issue 17 blocks annexation for a 1,000 MW Amazon data center and raises questions about a 250 MW Prologis facility under construction; Piqua OH charter ban passed with 67% (planned Meta site); Oregon OH caps data centers at 25 MW (Vantage proposal); Sunbury OH ban on facilities of 25 MW or more won 78% (Amazon's $2bn plan); Effingham County GA board unanimously delayed the site-plan decision on OpenAI's Project Camellia to Nov 17 and will discuss a moratorium.

items.name: Democrats' midterm gains put US data centre boom under pressure
items.source: The National, 2026-11-05 (own analysis of Cleanview data); corroborated by progressiverobot.com 2026-11-04
items.headline: Democrats' midterm gains put US data centre boom under pressure
items.candidate_dial: GW deferral (state-level moratorium pledges; pledges, not enacted)
items.claim: Democrats flipped five governorships (Texas, Georgia, Ohio, Iowa, Nevada) in states holding 37% of planned US data-centre capacity (Texas alone 22.8%); incoming Texas governor Gina Hinojosa promised an immediate construction moratorium and the Georgia and Ohio winners pledged pauses on large data centres; voters in 38 local jurisdictions across 10 states approved nearly every moratorium among at least 41 measures.
items.note: pre-election context (Bisnow 2026-11-01, citing Morgan Stanley): 284 data centers totalling more than 33 GW at risk in Texas, Pennsylvania and Georgia pending the state races

items.headline: Finnish data centre projects stall over proposed grid access law
items.claim: Scale42 paused its planned liquid-cooled AI data centre in Kitee because a proposed Electricity Market Act change would put it in the third of four grid-queue categories with no connection assessment until the end of next year. No MW printed.

items.source: 404K Research Substack - secondary, items printed without event dates
items.headline: 456X Morning Brief Nov 5: Microsoft lease-payment deferral and declined capacity (undated reports)
items.claim: Brief says payments under Microsoft's reported five-year $9.7bn IREN lease at Childress, originally slated for Q3, were pushed into later periods, and that Microsoft reportedly turned down about 500 MW of Nscale-owned capacity in Ward County while keeping a ~240 MW lease at the adjacent site. items.source: The Next Web; KuCoin flash 2026-11-02 - secondary (Axios original unreadable)
items.headline: OpenAI 'Grid Protectors': pledges up to 1 GW of demand response at Georgia campus
items.candidate_dial: GW deferral (demand response, not a capacity deferral)
items.claim: OpenAI pledged to cut demand at its planned 3.2 GW Effingham County, GA campus by up to 1 GW when the grid needs relief and to pay the full cost of lines and service; terms to be negotiated per site.

items.name: US Treasury shifts language, opening door to auction size changes
items.source: Reuters via 933thedrive.com syndication; corroborated by Saxo Market Quick Take 2026-11-05 - secondary
items.headline: US Treasury shifts language, opening door to auction size changes
items.candidate_dial: auction / supply (refunding guidance; no tail - no coupon auction held yet)
items.claim: Treasury kept next week's refunding at $125bn ($58bn 3y, $42bn 10y, $25bn 30y) but dropped 'at least' from its guidance, now expecting coupon and FRN sizes unchanged 'for the next several quarters'; dealers read it as opening the door to smaller long-dated issuance in 2027. US 10y fell 7bp to 4.89%.
